findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Statutory override on pooled fund accounting extended to April 2029, addressing contingency that prompted £5m reserve setup
findings.detail: The Government has extended the statutory override allowing councils to spread gains and losses on pooled investment funds over multiple years rather than recognizing them immediately. The extension runs until 1 April 2029 for investments in place before 1 April 2024. The MCA had set up a £5m reserve to mitigate the impact if the override had not been extended; that contingency has now been addressed.
findings.matters: The accounting treatment of unrealised investment losses affects financial reporting and the contingency reserves authorities must hold; the extension removes an immediate risk to usable reserves and reduces contingency planning burden.
findings.figures: £5m reserve had been set aside; statutory override extended to 1 April 2029
findings.quote: The statutory override will be extended up until the 1st April 2029 for investments already in place before 1st April 2024. The MCA had set up a reserve of £5m to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Mayoral Combined Authority holds no loans and has no underlying need to borrow for capital expenditure
findings.detail: As at 31 July 2026, the MCA held no loans outstanding. The authority has no underlying need to borrow long-term to fund capital expenditure. Short-term borrowing may be used only to cover unplanned cash flow shortages as they arise.
findings.matters: Many councils are dependent on borrowing for capital schemes; this authority's position indicates strong cash management and capital position. Lenders assess debt dependency as a key credit risk indicator.
findings.figures: £0m loans outstanding as at 31 July 2026; £450.2m invested funds available
findings.quote: The Mayoral Combined Authority does not currently have any underlying need to borrow long term to fund capital expenditure. As at 31st July 2026 the Mayoral Combined Authority held no loans.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Strategic pooled funds holding £49.1m show £2.8m unrealised capital loss but generate 4.5% annual return supporting services
findings.detail: The MCA holds £49.1m in externally managed strategic pooled funds showing £2.8m of unrealised capital loss at fair value (down from purchase value of £51.956m). These funds are generating an average total return of 4.5%, which is used to support services in-year, with cumulative income return since purchase of £11.384m.
findings.matters: Finance directors need to understand mark-to-market exposure in investment portfolios, particularly where unrealised losses exist; indicates portfolio volatility from recent market shocks including the Iran war and energy price spikes.
findings.figures: £2.8m unrealised loss on £49.1m invested (5.4% loss); 4.5% average annual return; £11.384m income return since purchase
findings.quote: These funds are generating an average total return of 4.5% which is used to support services in year, and £2.8m of unrealised capital loss

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Full-year investment income forecast at £16.7m against budget of £16.1m, a positive variance of £0.6m
findings.detail: The MCA expects to achieve a forecast year-end outturn of £16.7m for investment income against a full-year budget of £16.1m, representing a positive variance of £0.6m (3.7%). The report states this results from the Mayoral Combined Authority's successful treasury strategy and investment decisions.
findings.matters: Investment income is a key source of funding for services; outperformance of this scale indicates competent cash and investment management and provides additional resources.
findings.figures: £16.7m forecast vs £16.1m budget = £0.6m variance; portfolio average return 4.3%
findings.quote: The full year budget for 2026-27 investment income is £16.1m and following the Mayoral Combined Authority's successful treasury strategy and investment decisions, will expect to achieve a forecast year end outturn position of £16.7m which is a positive variance of £0.6m

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Internal Audit Plan
findings.headline: Internal control framework assessed as satisfactory with no significant policy breaches or systemic fraud failures in 2025/26
findings.detail: The Head of Audit & Assurance assessed the 2025/26 internal control framework as satisfactory, consistent with the prior year. No significant breaches of financial regulations or contract standing orders were identified, no systemic fraud failures occurred, and no fundamental control breakdowns affected business-critical functions.
findings.matters: Overall control environment assessment is the baseline indicator of governance quality and fraud risk; satisfactory rating provides assurance that internal controls remain adequate
findings.figures: 96% of prior year audit recommendations implemented (65 of 68); no fraud incidents or whistleblowing submissions in 2025/26
findings.quote: we are reporting the state of the internal control framework as satisfactory based on our audit opinions and delivery of the 2025/26 Annual Internal Audit Plan.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Internal Audit Plan
findings.headline: Grant certifications totalling £31.8 million all passed without significant issues identified
findings.detail: Internal audit reviewed and certified five grant streams in 2025/26 totalling £31.8 million: Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund (two consortia totalling £30.2 million), Bus Service Operators Grant (£1.1 million), Growth Hub (£380,000) and Local Industrial Decarbonisation Fund (£66,000). All certifications passed without significant issues.
findings.matters: Large volume of grant funding properly managed and independently certified indicates compliance capability and reduces reputational and financial risk for the authority and grant providers
findings.figures: £31.8 million total: SHDF Consortium 1 £15,280,053, SHDF Consortium 2 £14,944,700, BSOG £1,147,621, Growth Hub £380,000, LIDF £66,003
findings.quote: For all grants reviewed, no significant issues were identified, and we were able to provide independent assurance that WECA had complied with grant expenditure terms and conditions

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Internal Audit Plan
findings.headline: Organisational Improvement Programme required significant unplanned audit resource and continues subject to quarterly audit oversight
findings.detail: Audit of the OIP governance was unplanned work requiring significant internal audit resource during 2025/26. The audit achieved Reasonable Assurance, follow-up recommendations were all implemented, but internal audit has retained ongoing observer status at quarterly OIP Board meetings. A further audit of OIP delivery against objectives is scheduled for 2026/27.
findings.matters: Ongoing quarterly audit oversight of an organizational programme reflects sustained authority concern about governance of this initiative; unplanned audit work mid-year indicates governance issues were identified requiring close monitoring
findings.figures: Quarterly oversight continuing; further review scheduled 2026/27
findings.quote: Requests for unplanned work were received in year, with one particular piece of work relating to the Organisational Improvement Programme, requiring a significant and ongoing amount of Internal Audit resource.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Internal Audit Plan
findings.headline: Mobility-as-a-Service project audit recommendations remain partially implemented 18 months after initial identification
findings.detail: The 2024/25 audit of the MaaS project identified seven recommendations. Follow-up review in January 2026 found four fully implemented, but one high-priority recommendation (Innovation Project Methodology) and two medium-priority recommendations (Project Documentation and Risk Analysis Reporting) remain only partially implemented. Revised follow-up is scheduled for August 2026.
findings.matters: Persistent unresolved audit findings on project governance indicate control weakness in major project delivery and suggest difficulty implementing required improvements over an extended period
findings.figures: Four of seven recommendations implemented; one high and two medium priority outstanding as of January 2026 follow-up
findings.quote: The 2024/25 audit of Mobility as a Service Project Management was followed up in January 2026, with four of seven recommendations confirmed as implemented. One high priority and two medium priority recommendations originally followed up were noted as partially implemented and in progress.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: All four Director-level posts successfully recruited; strengthens leadership stability during organisational restructure
findings.detail: All four Director roles have been successfully recruited, providing strengthened leadership and organisational stability during the Target Operating Model restructure. This outcome is cited as a key mitigation against workforce capacity and retention risks during a period of significant organisational change.
findings.matters: Leadership continuity and successful recruitment at director level are important indicators of organisational stability during restructuring. Full staffing of senior leadership roles supports delivery capability and reduces leadership continuity risk during a period of uncertainty.
findings.figures: Four Director posts recruited
findings.quote: Successful recruitment of all four Director roles, providing strengthened leadership and stability across the organisation

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: Mayoral Capacity Funding received £0.5m above forecast in 2025/26; deployed to support delivery capacity
findings.detail: The MCA received Mayoral Capacity Funding higher than forecast in 2025/26: £1.5m actual against £1m budgeted. This additional £0.5m is being utilised to support delivery capacity and mitigate short-term resource pressures during the Target Operating Model organisational restructure.
findings.matters: One-off funding windfalls help absorb immediate pressures but are not sustainable solutions to structural funding constraints. This provides near-term relief but does not address the underlying real-terms erosion of core funding.
findings.figures: £1.5m actual versus £1m forecast; additional £0.5m
findings.quote: Utilisation of higher-than-expected Mayoral Capacity Funding (MCF) in 2025/26 (£1.5m vs £1m forecast) to support delivery capacity and mitigate short-term resource pressure

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: Mayor submitted application for Established Strategic Authority status; approval would unlock integrated settlement and multi-year funding certainty
findings.detail: Mayor Helen Godwin officially submitted the MCA's application for Established Strategic Authority status to government in June 2026, following Committee support on 5 June. Achievement of this status would provide access to integrated settlement funding, consolidated funding streams, greater local flexibility, simplified accountability arrangements, and increased funding certainty through multi-year settlements aligned to Spending Review periods.
findings.matters: Transition from current annual allocations to an integrated multi-year settlement would substantially improve financial predictability and medium-term sustainability. A peer finance director or lender tracking this authority would see approval as a major structural improvement to funding stability.
findings.figures: Application submitted June 2026
findings.quote: Mayor Helen Godwin has officially submitted the MCA application for Established Authority status to government, following support from Committee on 5 June

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement delivery risk improved significantly; £141m TCR funding secured and deadline extended to 2029
findings.detail: The CRSTS programme risk score reduced substantially from inherent 25 to 15 and residual 12 to 10, reflecting improved delivery confidence. A rebaselining exercise completed autumn 2025 was approved January 2026. Crucially, £141m of Transport for City Regions funding has been committed to complete the CRSTS programme by March 2029, extending the deadline from the previous 2027 target. Enhanced governance established through CRSTS Board in 2025.
findings.matters: A multi-year major capital programme underspend and deadline miss would trigger reputational damage and loss of future government funding. Secured funding and extended deadline represent resolution of a previously critical delivery risk.
findings.figures: Gross risk score reduced from 25 to 15; residual from 12 to 10; £141m TCR funding; deadline extended to March 2029
findings.quote: Rebase line committed approval of overprogramming schemes as well as £141m of TCR funding to complete CRSTS programme

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: Bristol Temple Quarter £95m Homes England scheme facing cost escalation; alternative funding for overruns being sourced
findings.detail: The Bristol Temple Quarter Phase 1 programme has £95m from Homes England and over £10m from the MCA's Investment Fund. Identified risks include cost escalation on remaining infrastructure projects. The MCA is in liaison with partners to source alternative funding for a Southern entrance cost overrun, subject to Committee approval. A new Head of Regeneration was appointed in June 2026 to strengthen the client role.
findings.matters: A £95m scheme requiring additional funding to cover cost overruns signals delivery and financial control challenges. Unsourced alternative funding indicates the overrun has already materialised and requires immediate resolution.
findings.figures: £95m Homes England grant; MCA invested over £10m
findings.quote: Potential for cost escalation once contractors are appointed on the remaining infrastructure projects funded through the Homes England grant, which may require additional MCA support

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: Global economic and inflation risk escalated to 2nd position on Corporate Risk Register; inherent score increased from 16 to 20
findings.detail: Global economic uncertainty driven by geopolitical instability and financial market volatility has escalated in the risk assessment. The inherent risk score increased from 16 to 20, moving this risk to 2nd position on the Corporate Risk Register. Rising global fuel prices are intensifying cost pressures across transport, supply chains and service delivery. The MCA is undertaking project rebaselining work to account for inflationary impacts on capital programme affordability.
findings.matters: Escalating cost pressures and widespread rebaselining work signal that earlier project cost assumptions are outdated. A peer finance director would recognise this as evidence that capital schemes are under delivery cost pressure and timelines may slip.
findings.figures: Inherent risk score increased from 16 to 20; risk moved to 2nd position on register
findings.quote: Rising global fuel prices are intensifying cost pressures across transport systems, supply chains, and service delivery, contributing to inflation and increasing the cost of project delivery, particularly within the MCA's capital programme

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 16 - Corporate Risk Register July 26
findings.headline: Devolution Deal settlement of £30m per year has no inflation uplift; combined with Investment Fund misalignment, reduces real-terms delivery capacity
findings.detail: The MCA's core funding is a fixed nominal £30m per year over 30 years with no inflation protection. Prior Investment Fund underspends have been absorbed, creating timing misalignment between available annual funding and committed expenditure. Together these reduce effective spending power and constrain the Authority's ability to deliver its capital programme and strategic priorities.
findings.matters: A lender assessing financial sustainability must understand whether core funding is adequate and protected against inflation. Fixed nominal funding in an inflationary environment erodes purchasing power and signals declining real-terms resources available for delivery over time.
findings.figures: £30m per year over 30 years with no inflation uplift
findings.quote: There is a risk that structural funding constraints, inflationary pressure and the timing of available resources reduce the MCA's capacity to deliver its investment programme and strategic priorities

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - MCA Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Authority held no debt at 31 March 2026; investment balances of £452.6m down £9.7m from prior year
findings.detail: The authority has no underlying need for long-term borrowing to fund capital expenditure and held no loans at year-end. Investment balances declined by £9.7m over the year, reflecting drawdowns for operational spending. The credit quality of the portfolio remained strong with A+ rating; £374.2m was invested in banks and local authorities.
findings.matters: Absence of debt means no refinancing risk, no rate reset exposure, and financial flexibility; balance decline is modest and consistent with normal cash deployment
findings.figures: £0m debt, £452.6m investments (down from £462.3m), A+ portfolio credit rating
findings.quote: As at 31 st March 2026 the Mayoral Combined Authority held no loans.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - MCA Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Authority maintains £5m reserve due to uncertainty over extension of statutory override on pooled investment valuations beyond April 2029
findings.detail: Current accounting regulations allow councils to smooth gains and losses on pooled investment funds through a statutory override set to expire on 1 April 2029. If not extended, the authority would face potential charges to reserves from unrealised losses already embedded in the portfolio (such as the £4m capital loss shown this year). The authority has set aside a £5m reserve to mitigate this forward-looking risk.
findings.matters: If the override lapses, a large charge to reserves could be triggered, materially affecting the authority's financial position and requiring advance planning or provision to absorb the impact
findings.figures: £5m reserve, override expiry date 1 April 2029, £4m portfolio losses already embedded
findings.quote: In view of the fact that the override may not be extended past 2029 the Mayoral Combined authority has decided to maintain this reserve

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - MCA Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Pooled fund investments of £52m recorded £4.0m aggregate capital loss despite 4.7% average income return
findings.detail: Strategic investments across property funds (CCLA £10m purchase declining to £8.9m fair value; Fundamentum REIT £5m purchase declining to £3m fair value), equity and bond funds show capital erosion across the portfolio. Fundamentum Social Housing REIT declined most steeply by £1.952m. The authority maintains these holdings based on confidence in medium-to-long-term returns.
findings.matters: Capital value deterioration reduces the real investment base even as income generation holds up; signals headwinds in commercial property and diversified asset markets that could persist
findings.figures: £52m invested across pooled funds, aggregate capital loss £4.007m, Fundamentum REIT loss £1.952m, average income return 4.7%
findings.quote: in 2025-26 provided an average total return of 4.7%. In light of their performance over the medium-long term, investment in these funds has been maintained.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - MCA Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Bank rate cuts to 3.75% will reduce investment income to 3.75-4.0% in 2026-27, down from 4.6% achieved this year
findings.detail: The Bank of England cut rates progressively during 2025-26 from 4.50% to 4.25% (May 2025), then to 4.00% (August 2025), and finally to 3.75% (December 2025). The authority expects this to flow through to lower returns on cash and short-dated investments next year, materially reducing the income windfall that benefited 2025-26.
findings.matters: Forecast income reduction of roughly 20% requires planning for reduced cash generation available for authority priorities without corresponding spending adjustments
findings.figures: Bank rate 4.50% → 4.00% → 3.75%; expected 2026-27 returns of 3.75-4.00% vs 4.6% achieved in 2025-26
findings.quote: Following the reduction in Bank rates during 2025-26, the Mayoral Combined Authority will expect to receive lower income (3.75% to 4.00% from its cash and short-dated investments, including money market funds in 2026/27).

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - MCA Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Investment income of £22.3m outperformed budget by £7.2m, with average return of 4.6% beating SONIA benchmark of 4.2%
findings.detail: The authority's investment portfolio generated £22.9m in gross interest over the year. After ringfencing income for the Revolving Investment Fund, the MCA's outturn was £22.3m against a budgeted £15.1m—a favourable variance of £7.2m. This was achieved while maintaining a diversified portfolio of £452.6m across banks, local authorities, money market funds and pooled investments.
findings.matters: A £7.2m windfall on investment income provides resources to support authority priorities or build reserves without requiring spending cuts or additional borrowing
findings.figures: £22.3m outturn vs £15.1m budget, £7.2m favourable variance, 4.6% average return vs 4.2% SONIA benchmark
findings.quote: Gross interest earned on all investments for April 2025 to March 2026 was £22.9m. Interest earned for RIF is ringfenced to those funds, giving rise to an income outturn for the West of England Mayoral Combined Authority activities of £22.3m v £15.1m budget, a favourable variance of £7.2m.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 15A - Annual Audit Report - Ext Audit
findings.headline: Draft 2024/25 financial statements published 2 July 2025, two weeks after statutory deadline, due to accessibility requirements; unqualified opinion issued 8 December 2025.
findings.detail: Authority missed 30 June 2025 deadline for publishing draft financial statements. Delay attributed to ensuring document was fully accessible before publication. Unformatted accounts were ready ahead of deadline. Audit commenced late June 2025 as Phase 1 priority to enable team to move to Phase 2 audits in September. Audit Findings Report presented to Audit Committee December 2025; unqualified opinion issued 8 December 2025. Auditors identified numerous audit adjustments requiring correction in final version, along with disclosure changes to improve presentation.
findings.matters: Missed statutory deadline indicates potential capacity or planning issues in finance team; late publication delays external audit, creating compressed audit timeline; numerous audit adjustments suggest financial reporting control environment remains weak; delayed audit opinion affects market perception of timeliness and financial position clarity.
findings.figures: 2 July 2025 publication (deadline 30 June 2025); audit opinion issued 8 December 2025
findings.quote: The Authority published its draft 2024/25 financial statements on the 2 July 2025, just missing the 30 June 2025 deadline. Delays were due to the need to ensure the document was fully accessible.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 15A - Annual Audit Report - Ext Audit
findings.headline: General reserves rebuilt to 5% of budgeted revenue expenditure target through £2.9m transfer in 2024/25 following £1.2m underspend.
findings.detail: Authority delivered £1.2m underspend in 2024/25 which funded £2.9m transfer to General Reserve, bringing balance above the 5% budgeted revenue expenditure target. Prior recommendation on reserve levels is now closed. Additional £3.6m transferred to Programme Risk Reserve to cover capital delivery slippage as capital programme accelerates. Balanced budget set for 2025/26.
findings.matters: Rebuilding reserves to recommended level strengthens financial resilience for unforeseen pressures; demonstrates capacity to manage revenue volatility; provides buffer for cash flow impacts as capital programme accelerates; previous audit recommendation now closed shows improved financial discipline.
findings.figures: £1.2m underspend 2024/25; £2.9m transfer to General Reserve; £3.6m transfer to Programme Risk Reserve; reserves now at 5% target
findings.quote: The Authority reported a £1.2m underspend for the year 2024/25 which allowed it to make a £2.9 transfer to the General Reserve. This took the balance above the 5% budgeted revenue expenditure target enabling us to close our prior year recommendation to this effect.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 15A - Annual Audit Report - Ext Audit
findings.headline: Investment income increasingly relied upon for core costs including staffing, but cash available for investment will decline as capital programme accelerates.
findings.detail: Investment income has become an important element supporting organisation's core costs. As capital programme moves from planning to delivery phases and cash balances draw down, investment income will reduce. This cost pressure will need to be mitigated through efficiencies in medium-term financial strategy. Authority planning £1.7m reduction in core costs to fund organisational improvement programme.
findings.matters: Investment income is volatile and depends on cash holdings and prevailing rates; declining availability signals need for operational cost reduction; if staffing costs cannot be reduced to match income decline, budget pressures will emerge; dependency on investment income for staffing is a structural risk if capital programme accelerates.
findings.figures: £1.7m planned reduction in core costs
findings.quote: Investment income has become an important element in supporting the organisation's core costs, including staffing. As the organisation develops, more projects within the Capital Programme move from planning to delivery phases and will start to draw down and reduce cash balances available for investment. The Authority recognises that this will create a cost pressure that will have to be mitigated through efficiencies in the MTFS.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 15A - Annual Audit Report - Ext Audit
findings.headline: Transport Levy shortfall of £1.898m in 2025/26 to be covered by reserve drawdown with sustainability of bus services dependent on future commercial model.
findings.detail: Authority is transitioning from short-term risk management through reserve drawdown to longer-term sustainability. Future funding for bus services identified as key area with necessary trade-off between affordability of levy to constituent councils and service level. Authority working to develop sustainable service funded primarily by local levy. Medium-term financial strategy sets out how service efficiencies will mitigate future funding shortfalls.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted £1.898m shortfall indicates Transport Levy revenue risk; reliance on reserve drawdown in 2025/26 reduces financial flexibility; commercial bus services are discretionary spending that could be cut if funding cannot be secured; future sustainability depends on success of local levy model which is untested.
findings.figures: £1.898m Transport Levy shortfall in 2025/26
findings.quote: WECA is managing short-term financial risks through planned reserve use, including covering a £1.898m shortfall in the Transport Levy for 2025/26.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 15A - Annual Audit Report - Ext Audit
findings.headline: City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement programme (£616.4m, due March 2027) significantly behind schedule with 87% of value still to deliver at start of 2024/25.
findings.detail: Internal Audit review gave limited assurance on CRSTS governance. At start of 2024/25, 87% of project value still to deliver in 3 years with doubt about supply chain capacity. Forecast capital spend in 2025/26 nearly doubles to £204m from £113.6m in 2024/25. New governance arrangements implemented June 2024 onwards; Director of Infrastructure departed; new Executive Director of Transport now in post. Auditors assess significant weakness in governance, recognising delivery carries heightened risk requiring demonstrated progress over next 12 months.
findings.matters: £616.4m is material funding dependent on timely delivery; programme underpinned by government funding agreement with penalty risk for non-delivery; acceleration plan creates short-term cash flow pressure and delivery risk; if constituent councils cannot deliver to timetable, repayment obligations or reputational damage to authority's credibility with government funders.
findings.figures: £616.4 million total allocation; 87% of value undelivered at start 2024/25; forecast capital spend £113.6m (2024/25) to £204m (2025/26)
findings.quote: at the start of 2024/25, 87% of the value of projects within the CRSTS Programme had still to be delivered in the remaining three years of the programme and there was some doubt in the capacity of the supply chain to be able to deliver the majority of projects over the same reduced period of time.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 15A - Annual Audit Report - Ext Audit
findings.headline: Significant weakness in governance arrangements: legacy issues, process failures on contractor and officer appointments, and £475,713 in severance costs in 2024/25.
findings.detail: Two contractors were appointed without proper procurement processes in breach of contract procedure rules. Senior officer appointments in 2023 were made without proper Committee approval, confirmed in breach of the Constitution by KC legal advice. Departures of four senior officers (Interim CEO, Interim Monitoring Officer, Strategic Director of Resources, Strategic Director of Infrastructure) resulted in exit packages and settlements totalling £475,713 excluding VAT. Although the Best Value notice was lifted in March 2025 and new Mayor elected May 2025, auditors assess residual significant weakness remains.
findings.matters: Governance failures expose the authority to legal challenge and reputational damage; recurring severance costs indicate dysfunction in performance management and staff relations; new Mayor and leadership offer opportunity to embed sustainable improvement, but effectiveness over next 12 months will determine financial and reputational risk.
findings.figures: £475,713 severance and settlement costs (exc. VAT); Best Value notice lifted March 2025; new Mayor elected May 2025
findings.quote: further significant cost to the Authority...resulted in further significant cost to the Authority. We note that during 2024/25 there were other settlements to conclude historic cases relating to the departure of other former senior employees...took together, have resulted in further significant cost to the Authority.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26
findings.headline: MCA seeking government agreement on sustainable core funding as current annual allocations cannot cover permanent staff costs
findings.detail: The paper identifies that core staffing costs are not covered by permanent funding sources and are currently reliant on treasury management income. The authority states it will continue lobbying government to establish sustainable core funding for Combined Authorities beyond the current annual allocation model. This reflects a structural funding gap that cannot be closed through existing grant and levy income streams.
findings.matters: Authority has identified unsustainable funding model for permanent operational capacity; success or failure of government funding case is critical to organizational stability; unsuccessful lobbying would force staffing reductions or require sustained treasury income above current forecasts.
findings.figures: Core staffing currently dependent on variable treasury income; permanent funding gap not quantified but implicit in core cost coverage
findings.quote: The West of England MCA will continue to put forward a case to government to establish sustainable core funding for Combined Authorities beyond the current annual allocations.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26
findings.headline: Capital Transport programme £50.8m rephased to later years after City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement re-baselining exercise
findings.detail: Capital forecast £209.3m versus budget £221.2m (£11.9m, 5% underspend). Transport shows the largest variance at £50.8m (24% of transport budget) driven by rephasing of City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement and Rail programmes following re-baselining to establish firm delivery plans through March 2029. Concurrently, optimism bias provision of £39.3m is being released as projects progress and risk reduces, though this release offsets only part of the rephasing.
findings.matters: Major transport infrastructure schemes are being rescheduled to later years; completion timescales extending; release of £39.3m risk provision alongside reprofiling suggests delivery confidence varying across the programme.
findings.figures: Capital forecast £209.3m vs £221.2m budget (£11.9m variance, 5%); Transport variance £50.8m (24%); optimism bias release £39.3m (71% of original provision)
findings.quote: The CRSTS programme has been through a re-baselining exercise to establish firm delivery plans for the completion of the settlement over through to March 2029. This ensures resources are directed towards maximising delivery within the available funding window.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26
findings.headline: Adult Skills Fund grant reduced £1.2m from Department for Education; shortfall absorbed from reserves
findings.detail: Adult Skills Fund budget of £17.185m forecast at £15.979m—a reduction of £1.206m (7%) reflecting a grant reduction from the Department for Education. The authority is funding the shortfall from reserves rather than reducing service delivery. This sits within a broader pattern of grant reductions (Youth Trailblazer £0.9m, UKSPF £0.8m), totalling £10.1m (9%) in grant funding reductions.
findings.matters: Confirmed central government funding has reduced mid-year; authority is using reserves to avoid service cuts, reducing financial flexibility for future emerging pressures.
findings.figures: Adult Skills Fund £1.206m reduction (7%); sits within £10.1m total grant funding variance (9% of £112m budget)
findings.quote: Adult Skills down £1.2m, there has been a reduction in grant from the DoE. The shortfall has been funded from reserves.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26

findings.detail: General reserves forecast to reach £9.6m at end of 2025/26, representing 5.6% of expenditure and exceeding the minimum target of £8.7m (5% of expenditure). The authority added £1.9m to general reserves during 2025/26. This is described as strengthening financial resilience, though it must be viewed alongside forward transport levy pressures and increased Programme Risk Reserve of £10m for capital delivery risks.
findings.matters: Authority has built general reserves above recommended minimum, providing buffer against emerging financial risks and supporting capital programme protection; demonstrates financial discipline in reserve building, though forward pressures constrain availability.

findings.quote: The current forecast indicates that general reserves will stand at £9.6m by the end of 2025/26, compared to a minimum target of £8.7m. This represents a strengthening of the Authority's financial resilience above the recommended level.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26
findings.headline: Treasury management income £6.5m above budget but currently funding core staffing costs in a manner the authority identifies as unsustainable
findings.detail: Treasury income forecast at £21.8m versus £15.3m budget, a positive variance of £6.5m (42%), from stronger cash balances and higher interest rates than assumed. However, the paper explicitly states this income is being used to cover core staffing cost increases and flags this as unsustainable. As cash balances decline with ongoing capital delivery or if interest rates fall, core staffing will be at risk without alternative permanent funding sources.
findings.matters: Core operating staff costs are not covered by permanent funding sources; authority is exposed to interest rate and cash balance volatility; staffing reductions may become forced if treasury income declines, affecting organizational capacity.
findings.figures: Treasury income £21.8m forecast vs £15.3m budget; £6.5m positive variance (42-43%)
findings.quote: Treasury Management income is currently being used to fund the increase in core staffing costs, which is not a sustainable approach. As balances decline with ongoing delivery or if interest rates fall, the available funding for core costs will decrease, requiring the authority to either reduce staff or identify alternative funding sources.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26
findings.headline: Transport levy forecast to require £1.2m reserve drawdown versus £187k budgeted, with material forward risk to 2026/27 service continuity
findings.detail: Q3 forecast shows transport levy requiring £1.229m drawn from reserves against budget of £187k—a £1.042m adverse movement (557%). Overspends in concessionary fares and supported bus services are driving the variance. The paper explicitly flags a material forward risk: reserves may need to be fully utilised in 2026/27 to sustain service provision, leaving no reserves available for 2027/28.
findings.matters: Transport is the largest cost pressure in the levy structure; forward depletion of reserves needed to meet statutory transport provision creates significant risk to service continuity; if reserves are exhausted in 2026/27, no funding buffer remains for 2027/28 pressures.
findings.figures: Forecast levy drawdown £1.229m; budgeted £187k; 2026/27 forward risk explicitly flagged as material
findings.quote: There is a material risk that reserves may need to be fully utilised to sustain service provision, even with the 2026/27 Bus Grant award (£14.1m). Should this occur, there would be no reserves available to support services into 2027/28, leaving future provision exposed to further funding uncertainty.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast 2025-26

The budget assumed 100% learner completion and achievement of outcomes in line with Department for Education grant conditions. The Q3 forecast reflects lower than anticipated learner enrolment and take-up, indicating a material gap between programme design assumptions and actual market demand.
findings.matters: Skills programme underperformance against design suggests either the programme design is misaligned with learner needs or market demand is weaker than forecast; this affects delivery of public skills investment objectives and may signal wider skills policy issues.
findings.figures: Skills Bootcamps £8.9m variance; Economy & Skills total directorate variance £13.3m (25% of £52.4m budget)
findings.quote: The Skills Bootcamps variance reflects the gap between the original budget assumption — based on 100% learner completion and delivery of outcomes in line with Department for Education grant conditions—and the current forecast, which assumes lower than anticipated learner enrolment and take-up.

findings.detail: The auditors issued an unqualified opinion on West of England Combined Authority's 2024/25 financial statements on 8 December 2025. However, the formal audit certificate required by the Local Audit and Accountability Act 2014 cannot be issued until three items are resolved: completion of the National Audit Office's audit of the Whole of Government Accounts; resolution of an objection from a member of the public; and resolution of further communications impacting the auditors' role.
findings.matters: A lender or peer council needs to understand both the audit outcome (unqualified is positive) and what specific matters remain unresolved before formal sign-off, particularly a member of public objection which may indicate governance or compliance issues.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Corporate functions increase 19% (£3.3m) and staffing grows despite 16% reduction in delivery programme funding
findings.detail: Revenue funding for delivery programmes falls by £21.1m (16%) to £113.8m, primarily due to ending grants. However, corporate functions costs rise by £3.3m (19%) to £20.6m. The MCA explicitly states that 'while overall revenue funding reduces in 2026/27 as a number of large time-limited programmes had allocations revised down, the MCA's core operations do not reduce correspondingly'. Growth is driven by establishing the Organisational Improvement Programme team, increased HR capacity for transition to new target operating model, expansion of the Graduates programme, higher Minimum Revenue Position, and strengthening contract management and grant assurance capacity. The MCA is investing in internal capability to reduce reliance on external consultants.
findings.matters: A finance director watching organisational cost trends would note this countercyclical staffing growth: as grant-funded programmes shrink, permanent overhead is growing. While the MCA justifies this as investment in sustainability and new responsibilities, it raises questions about the proportion of the shrinking revenue base now devoted to administration versus delivery, and whether this trend is sustainable if revenue continues to decline.
findings.figures: Delivery programme funding: £134.9m (2025/26) to £113.8m (2026/27), -£21.1m (-16%). Corporate functions: £17.3m (2025/26) to £20.6m (2026/27), +£3.3m (+19%). Corporate Office increase (including OIP team): +£1.6m (+24%).
findings.quote: Growth in staffing should be viewed in this context. While overall revenue funding reduces in 2026/27 as a number of large time-limited programmes had allocations revised down, the MCA's core operations do not reduce correspondingly.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Transport Levy held at £21.9m through managed efficiencies despite inflation, but sustainability of levy structure under pressure
findings.detail: The Transport Levy, which funds bus and transport services across the region, increases by £1.6m (8%) to £21.9m for 2026/27, funded by proportional contributions from Bristol City Council, Bath & North East Somerset, South Gloucestershire, and North Somerset. The MCA states that operating costs are 'significantly impacted by inflationary pressures' yet has 'managed resources efficiently to sustain service levels under the current levy structure'. However, the MCA has committed jointly with Unitary Authorities to 'exploring a longer-term, strategic and equitable approach', signalling that the current model may not be sustainable without fundamental change. Collaborative planning with partner authorities is flagged as 'critical'.
findings.matters: Peers watching how other MCAs manage shared funding arrangements with constituent authorities would note this as a pressure point. A service held level only through efficiency gains, with parties committed to exploring alternatives, suggests the current funding mechanism cannot indefinitely absorb inflation. This risks future either reductions in service or calls for larger levy increases, both of which could affect constituent authorities' own budgets.
findings.figures: Transport Levy: £20.3m (2025/26) to £21.9m (2026/27), +£1.6m (+8%). Components: Bristol City Council £11.5m, Bath & North East Somerset £5.7m, South Gloucestershire £4.6m, North Somerset £1.8m.
findings.quote: Operating the Transport Levy continues to be significantly impacted by inflationary pressures. Despite these pressures, the organisation has managed resources efficiently to sustain service levels under the current levy structure.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Capital programme grows 27% to £262.6m as major transport schemes transition from design into construction phases; optimism bias of 24% (£82.6m) applied to forecasts
findings.detail: The capital budget grows by £55.6m (27%) to £262.6m, driven by City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS) schemes progressing into delivery. Key projects entering construction in 2026/27 include Bristol City Centre, A4 Portway, Bradley Stoke Way, A38 Thornbury, Bath City Centre, and rail projects including MetroWest schemes. The MCA has applied an optimism bias adjustment of 24% (£82.6m) to the raw project forecasts, explicitly to account for historical slippage and delivery delays. The paper acknowledges delays in governance, planning, tendering, and partner organisations' own capital slippage.
findings.matters: A lender financing or monitoring a council watches whether capital programmes are realistic and deliverable, especially when scaled up significantly. An optimism bias of 24% is substantial and signals the MCA's own assessment that raw forecasts tend to overestimate pace of spend. For cash flow, this means the £262.6m budget will likely spend slower than profiled, affecting treasury cash balances and income.
findings.figures: Capital expenditure: £206.9m (2025/26) to £262.6m (2026/27), +£55.6m (+27%). Optimism bias factor: £82.6m (24% of raw forecasts). Transport capital: £297.6m (up £107.2m). Rail projects (MetroWest 1, 2, Charfield): combined £128m.
findings.quote: the overall budget increases by £34.9m (9%) to £415.8m, driven by a £55.6m (27%) increase in the capital programme to £262.6m.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Revenue budget shrinks 12% (£20.7m) as time-limited grant programmes end; bus and skills funding each decline materially
findings.detail: Total revenue income falls from £173.9m to £153.2m in 2026/27, a 12% reduction. This is almost entirely driven by grant funding declining by £21.2m (19%), primarily two named programmes: bus funding down £14.8m as the Bus Service Improvement Plan ends, and Skills Bootcamp funding down £6.1m as that scheme restructures. The MCA explicitly states these are time-limited programme cycles and profiling changes, not structural cuts. However, the consequence is that the MCA's core revenue base has contracted, requiring either delivery reductions in bus and skills services (which are being offset by new grant), or reliance on other income sources to maintain activity.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would watch whether revenue is contracting due to temporary grant cycles (manageable with planning) or structural income loss. The MCA shows the detail here, which is useful; however, peers would also note that if the replacement grants (new Creative Places Growth programme, new Bus Grant) have different conditions or durations, income volatility may persist.
findings.figures: Grant funding: £109.9m (2025/26) to £88.8m (2026/27), -£21.2m (-19%). Bus funding decrease: £14.8m. Skills Bootcamp reduction: £6.1m. New Creative Places Growth programme: £25m over three years from April 2026.
findings.quote: Grant funding remains the MCA's primary source of revenue income and is forecast to reduce by £20.7m (12%) compared to the prior year. This reduction is primarily driven by a £14.8m decrease in funding for buses and a £6.1m reduction in Skills Bootcamp funding, reflecting the time-limited nature and profiling of specific programmes.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Reserves remain ranked lowest among all 11 Mayoral Combined Authorities despite planned strengthening
findings.detail: West of England's general and earmarked reserves stand at £31.6m or 12% of gross spend, ranking 10th out of 11 MCAs. Peer MCAs hold an average of £221m or 27% of spend. The MCA acknowledges this gap and has committed to strengthening reserves through planned transfers from improved 2025/26 treasury performance. However, the paper notes that reserve levels 'remain below those of other Mayoral Combined Authorities and the budget recognises the need for continued progress over the medium term'—a multi-year commitment rather than a near-term fix.
findings.matters: Reserve adequacy is a primary lens through which lenders assess financial resilience and flexibility. A reserve position significantly below peer group—and acknowledged as such by management—signals limited financial buffers for unforeseen pressures and constrained capacity to absorb income volatility or spending shocks. The commitment to rebuild over several years, not immediately, is itself the news.
findings.figures: West of England reserves: £31.6m (12% of gross spend), ranked 10 out of 11 MCAs. Other MCA average: £221.0m (27% of gross spend).
findings.quote: It highlights that we remain ranked amongst the lowest across all key metrics.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Treasury income forecast to decline despite 2026/27 budget rise, as capital drawdown accelerates and interest rates fall
findings.detail: Treasury income of £16.1m is budgeted for 2026/27, a slight rise from the 2025/26 budget of £15.1m. However, the MCA acknowledges that in-year 2025/26 treasury performance is currently running ahead of that budget. The 2026/27 forecast decline is driven by two factors: capital construction costs being drawn down as approved major projects (particularly CRSTS schemes) move into delivery phases, which reduces available cash balances; and assumptions of lower interest rates ahead. This creates a future income gap even as capital spending accelerates.
findings.matters: Lenders and peer finance directors need to track reliance on treasury income for core revenue. A declining income stream as capital programmes accelerate can force either reserve drawdown or spending reductions. The MCA's stated concern about this reliance signals awareness of the risk.
findings.figures: Treasury income: £15.1m (2025/26 budget) to £16.1m (2026/27 budget), +£1.0m, but forecast to decline from current in-year performance. Capital programme: £206.9m (2025/26) to £262.6m (2026/27), +£55.6m (27%).
findings.quote: Although strong returns are forecast for 2026/27, income is expected to decline as capital construction costs are drawn down for the approved Capital Programme and lower anticipated interest rates.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 08 - MCA Budget 2026-27 and MTFS
findings.headline: Business rates reset eliminates £2.2m income stream; MCA assumes £0 retained income for 2026/27 and draws on smoothing reserve
findings.detail: The national business rates reset and rebaselining has created uncertainty over retention income. The MCA has taken a prudent approach by assuming zero net retained income in 2026/27, down from £2.2m in 2025/26. To bridge this gap, the MCA will draw on its earmarked Business Rates Retention Smoothing Reserve, accepting that any growth above the rebaselined position confirmed in-year will reduce drawdown rather than fund new spending.
findings.matters: A lender watching cash flow needs to know whether income sources are stable or subject to sudden reset. A 100% reduction in a named income stream, replaced by reserve drawdown for an unknown duration, creates both near-term cash management risk and medium-term sustainability questions.
findings.figures: Business rates retained: £2.2m (2025/26) to £0 (2026/27), 100% reduction. Draw on Business Rates Retention Smoothing Reserve: £1.7m in 2026/27.
findings.quote: the MCA has taken a prudent planning assumption of £0 net retained business rates income within the core revenue budget for 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Item 07B - Draft Non-Treasury Strategies - App 2 Draft Non-treasury Inv Strategy 2627

findings.matters: This represents a significant new direct investment initiative with exposure to business credit risk and emerging net zero sector risks. The fund is expected to deploy capital across multiple businesses, making portfolio credit quality and diversification material considerations for lenders assessing the authority's investment portfolio.

findings.quote: The £10m will be 'cornerstone' capital investment into the Green Growth West Impact Fund to support net zero business growth, the creation of jobs and the region's ambition to be net zero by 2030.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 07B - Draft Non-Treasury Strategies - App 2 Draft Non-treasury Inv Strategy 2627
findings.headline: MCA states there are no immediate plans to borrow to fund planned service investments
findings.detail: All investments to date are funded from useable reserves, Investment Fund balances, and income received in advance of expenditure, with "no immediate plans to borrow". This contrasts with other councils that have used Public Works Loan Board borrowing to fund investment strategies.
findings.matters: The decision to fund investments entirely from reserves rather than through borrowing has implications for reserve depletion and medium-term financial sustainability. findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 07B - Draft Non-Treasury Strategies - App 2 Draft Non-treasury Inv Strategy 2627
findings.headline: Overall investment rate of return forecast to decline from 5.7% to 4.17% as treasury returns fall with interest rates
findings.detail: The MCA's blended investment return across all categories is forecast to decline from 5.7% in 2024/25 to 4.17% in 2026/27, a fall of 130 basis points. This is driven by declining treasury management returns (4.9% to 4.17%), reflecting lower prevailing interest rates. Service loan returns are expected to remain at 6.5% but represent a smaller share of the portfolio.
findings.matters: Investment returns contribute to the authority's net revenue position. The forecast decline affects medium-term budget planning and the financial contribution these investments can make to council operations.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 07B - Draft Non-Treasury Strategies - App 2 Draft Non-treasury Inv Strategy 2627
findings.headline: £6.5m loan committed to Bristol Temple Quarter regeneration with final terms still to be agreed
findings.detail: The MCA is an equal partner in Bristol Temple Quarter LLP (jointly with Homes England and Bristol City Council) and has committed to lend £6.5m to support regeneration. The document states the loan terms "still need to be agreed" with drawdown expected "sometime in 2026". This commits material funding while key terms including repayment period and interest rate remain undefined.
findings.matters: Committing to a £6.5m facility where principal terms have not been finalized is unusual. Lenders would want to understand the timeline for finalizing terms and the MCA's negotiating position, as undefined terms in major commitments can signal process or governance gaps.
findings.quote: The MCA will loan capital of £6.5m under terms which still need to be agreed and which is expected to be fully drawn down sometime in 2026.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 07B - Draft Non-Treasury Strategies - App 2 Draft Non-treasury Inv Strategy 2627
findings.headline: Service investment loan exposure forecast to grow to £19.5m by March 2027, including Bristol Temple Quarter and Green Growth Fund commitments
findings.detail: The MCA plans to deploy £19.5m in service loans by March 2027, up from minimal amounts currently. This includes £6.5m to Bristol Temple Quarter regeneration and £10m as cornerstone capital into the Green Growth West Impact Fund for net zero business growth. This represents a significant shift from treasury-style investments (deposits with high-grade counterparties) to direct lending to specific projects and businesses.
findings.matters: This shift materially changes the credit risk profile of the authority's portfolio. Direct lending to projects and businesses carries different risk characteristics than treasury investments. Lenders would assess the credit quality, diversification and loss-provisioning of these new exposures.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 06 - Treasury Management Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Investment income budget for 2026/27 falls to £13.7m (40% reduction) as portfolio contracts and interest rate cuts are forecast
findings.detail: The authority budgets investment income of £13.7m for 2026/27 based on average portfolio of £325m earning 4.17%, down from 2025/26 forecast of £22.5m on average portfolio earning 4.6%. The reduction reflects: (1) planned decline in investment holdings as capital grants are deployed to finance capital expenditure, with average portfolio falling from current £511m to £325m; and (2) expected interest rate falls, with Bank Rate remaining at 4.0% in November and forecast to cut to 3.75% in December 2025, compared to 4.5% at start of 2025.
findings.matters: Material decline in investment income from interest rate normalization will affect all councils' revenue budgets; finance directors need to plan for similar income reductions as rates fall and portfolio balances decline.
findings.figures: 2026/27 budget £13.7m on £325m average portfolio at 4.17%; 2025/26 forecast £22.5m; current holdings £510.9m (31 Oct 2025); Bank Rate currently 4.0%, forecast 3.75% by December 2025
findings.quote: The draft budget for the West of England Mayoral Combined Authority investment income in 2026/27 is predicated to be £13.7 million, based on an average investment portfolio of £325 million at an average interest rate of 4.17% and making an allowance for impairment as required.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 06 - Treasury Management Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Strategic pooled fund portfolio of £52m fell in value by £3.9m with Fundamentum Social Housing REIT declining £1.9m (38%)
findings.detail: Between March and October 2025, the authority's £52m strategic pooled fund holdings fell to £48m fair value, representing capital losses of £3.9m (7.6%). The largest loss was Fundamentum Social Housing REIT, down £1.9m from £5.0m to £3.1m (38%) with cumulative income of only £44k since purchase. Other material losses: CCLA Property Fund (£1.1m loss, 10.9%), Investec Diversified Income (£821k loss, 8.2%), Threadneedle Strategic Bond (£296k loss). M&G UK Income and Royal London funds recorded modest gains. The portfolio has generated £10.1m cumulative income since purchase, though insufficient to offset capital losses.
findings.matters: Finance directors need to understand capital volatility in strategic longer-term investments; the 38% loss on Fundamentum REIT and significant losses on property and fixed-income funds signal concentration risk in illiquid asset classes during market downturns.
findings.figures: Total pooled funds £51.9m purchase → £48.0m fair value (loss £3.9m, 7.6%); Fundamentum REIT £5.0m → £3.1m (loss £1.9m, 38%); CCLA Property £10.0m → £8.9m (loss £1.1m, 10.9%); Investec £10.0m → £9.2m (loss £821k, 8.2%); cumulative portfolio income £10.1m
findings.quote: The combination of the above had a marginal negative effect on the combined value of the Mayoral Combined Authority's strategic funds since March 2025.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 07A - Draft Non-Treasury Strategies - App 1 Draft MCA Capital Strategy 2627
findings.headline: Capital financing entirely from external sources (grants) with zero contribution from revenue, capital receipts, or borrowing
findings.detail: Table 2 shows all planned capital expenditure financed by external sources (government grants and other contributions), with zero planned inputs from revenue resources, capital receipts from asset sales, or new borrowing across the forecast period 2025/26 to 2028/29. This represents complete grant dependency for capital delivery.
findings.matters: Total reliance on grant funding for capital delivery means the authority has no internal financial flexibility to substitute or replace lost funding and must manage delivery risk if grant allocations are delayed or reduced.
findings.figures: 2025/26 actual: external sources £48.14m, capital receipts £0.000m, revenue resources £0.000m, debt £0.000m (same pattern forecast across all years)
findings.quote: All capital expenditure must be financed, either from external sources (government grants and other contributions), the Authority's own resources (revenue, reserves and capital receipts) or debt (borrowing, leasing and Private Finance Initiative).

findings.headline: Treasury investments planned to fall by £209.5m within one year, from £421.0m forecast (March 2026) to £211.5m budget (March 2027)
findings.detail: Near-term treasury investments are forecast at £369.0m as at 31 March 2026 but budgeted to fall to £159.0m by 31 March 2027—a reduction of £210m in liquid assets held in near-term instruments. Longer-term investments remain stable at £52.0m. This material drawdown of reserves signals capital deployment or cash outflow within a single financial year.
findings.matters: A near-£210m reduction in near-term liquid assets within twelve months indicates either accelerated capital spending or deliberate reserve depletion, affecting the authority's financial flexibility and liquidity headroom.
